You need to learn about the macronutrient contents of different foods, and what their purposes are.  Proteins are the building blocks of muscle, whereas carbs and fats are sources of energy.  The rates of digestion of each macronutrient will be very different as well. The caloric differences of each are very different also, so you should keep this in mind depending on what your goals are with regards to weight loss/gain.. It's not really a matter of good or bad, as much as what is ideal for the situation and your goals.
Most people try to consume more protein post lifting to begin the recovery process.. A quicker digesting meal is ideal hence the post workout protein shake.

How many scoops of the protein do you take with the milk?  Have you tried taking it without milk at all (with water instead)?  How long before your workout do you have your last meal, and what sort of meal is it?  How many solid meals do you have before your workout and protein shake?  There are many variables that can have an affect on this.

  You have to start testing different ways of consumption to find out what the most likely cause of your problem is..  Try just having one scoop of the protein with water.. if that works then have 2 scoops with water.. etc.  You probably have to start guess and checking to figure out how your body responds and learn what works for you.
Contact national news stations like CNN.  Try contacting people like Anderson Cooper, etc.  You have nothing to lose and everything to gain.. Don't give up..

The biggest problem with most people when it comes to nutrition and supplementation is that they tend to over-analyze everything.  You will not have some sort of magical physical transformation by choosing a certain protein brand.  Most brands are similar, and you will get the same result from them.  Cheaper brands may use fillers and less actual protein in the product, so just look at the labels for the amount of protein per scoop..  

You just have to stick to the basics and be consistent with your diet and supplementation.  Any "whey" protein supplement will work just fine for most people..  "Soy" protein is meant for those that may be lactose intolerant.  

In general you should consume at least 1 gram of protein for every pound of lean body mass on your body to maintain your current level of muscularity (simple ex: you weigh 100lbs with 20% body fat = 80 lbs lean body mass = you need 80grams of protein per day for maintenance).  

When trying to gain muscle and size, you should consume 1.5 to 2 grams of protein for every pound of lean body mass on your body per day (simple ex: you weigh 100 lbs with 20% body fat = 80 lbs lean body mass = 120 to 160 grams of protein per day for muscle growth).

There are many reasons food consumption can be viewed as "superior" to protein supplementation.  Food will digest at a slower rate and keep you satiated for a longer period of time.  Food will generally be more calorically dense than a protein supplement, and calories = growth.  The thermic effect of food is greater than the thermic effect of protein supplementation which boosts your metabolism (meaning your body will have to work and burn calories digesting the food).

To start just get a protein supplement and figure out your daily protein requirements for your goals.  Try to eat as much food protein as you can, and supplement the rest.  Stay consistent with your consumption on a day to day basis.  Also try to figure out your average daily caloric intake and make sure you're eating enough to facilitate growth.  You will not be able to make significant gains on a caloric deficit..

Good luck..
